newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to announce government changes soon.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to announce government changes soon.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, making his annual address to the Russian parliament on Thursday, said he would announce a shake-up in his government in the coming days.

"The time has come to restore order. The structure and composition of the government must be changed. New and competent people will come and I will announce these changes in the coming days," he said, speaking in a clear, confident voice.
Yeltsin, who looked grave and determined, gave no details on the impending reshuffle.

Speculation has raged in recent days about who might leave the government. Kremlin sources have said Yeltsin is likely to name liberal economist Anatoly Chubais, currently his chief-of-staff, to a powerful new post under Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin with sweeping powers to fight corruption.
The shake-up is seen as part of Yeltsin's strategy to reassert his authority and show that he is back in control after many months of absence from the Kremlin due to illness.
Chernomyrdin will chair a cabinet meeting later on Thursday which may give a clearer indication of who will leave the cabinet.
